messages.subject: Re: [knitr] Rendering a table in latex when a rowname starts with [
messages.subject_clean: [knitr] Rendering a table in latex when a rowname starts with [
messages.body_plain:
Turns out that I can't use ktable as it is not exported?

library(knitr)
ktable(tab)

complains that "ktable" function is not found.

knitr::ktable(tab) complains that ktable is not exported.

If someone has fixed this before, could you please comment?

Best regards,
Gopal

On Wednesday, December 31, 2014 9:17:41 AM UTC+2, Gopal Peddinti wrote:
> Thanks a lot Yihui for your prompt answer. I didn't know about this knitr::ktable function, thanks for the pointer.
>
> Best regards,
> Gopal
>
> On Tuesday, December 30, 2014 7:58:34 PM UTC+2, Yihui Xie wrote:
> > It is probably an xtable bug. I just tested knitr::kable(), and it did
> > not have the problem:
> >
> > \documentclass{article}
> >
> > \begin{document}
> >
> > <<results='asis'>>=
> > tab <- matrix(rnorm(4), nrow=2)
> > rownames(tab) <- c("a", "[b]c")
> > colnames(tab) <- c("p", "q")
> > library(knitr)
> > kable(tab)
> > @
> >
> > \end{document}
> >
> > I guess the best way to solve the problem is to ask xtable authors to
> > fix it. You can also set your sanitize.rownames.function as a global
> > option in R via options(), though.
> >
> > Regards,
> > Yihui
> > --
> > Yihui Xie <xiey...@gmail.com>
> > Web: http://yihui.name
> >
> >
> > On Tue, Dec 30, 2014 at 8:12 AM, Gopal Peddinti <cug...@gmail.com> wrote:
> > > Dear all,
> > >
> > > I am using knitr to produce PDF documents using pdflatex. I have to print a
> > > table which has chemical names as its rownames. One rowname starts with left
> > > square bracket [. I am trying to include this table in my knitr document
> > > using print(xtable(tab)), but latex fails to render this. Below I create a
> > > toy example to describe the issue. The following document doesn't render.
> > >
> > >
> > > \documentclass{article}
> > >
> > > \begin{document}
> > >
> > > <<results='asis'>>=
> > > tab <- matrix(rnorm(4), nrow=2)
> > > rownames(tab) <- c("a", "[b]c")
> > > colnames(tab) <- c("p", "q")
> > > library(xtable)
> > > print(xtable(tab))
> > > @
> > >
> > > \end{document}
> > >
> > > One dirty workaround I found was to insert a line change character at the
> > > beginning of the rowname that starts with [. That is, the following document
> > > renders correctly:
> > >
> > >
> > > \documentclass{article}
> > >
> > > \begin{document}
> > >
> > > <<results='asis'>>=
> > > tab <- matrix(rnorm(4), nrow=2)
> > > rownames(tab) <- c("a", "\n[b]c")
> > > colnames(tab) <- c("p", "q")
> > > library(xtable)
> > > print(xtable(tab))
> > > @
> > >
> > > \end{document}
> > >
> > > Therefore, in my real case the knitr code using this workaround is something
> > > like the following (which is just a generalization of the above by inserting
> > > \n wherever needed):
> > >
> > > \documentclass{article}
> > >
> > > \begin{document}
> > >
> > > <<results='asis'>>=
> > > tab <- matrix(rnorm(4), nrow=2)
> > > rownames(tab) <- c("a", "[b]c")
> > > colnames(tab) <- c("p", "q")
> > >
> > > ### I insert \n at the beginning of rownames that start with [
> > > rownames(tab) <- gsub("^\\[", "\n\\[", rownames(tab))
> > > library(xtable)
> > > print(xtable(tab))
> > > @
> > > \end{document}
> > >
> > > I tried to achieve this same workaround using sanitize.rownames.function as
> > > below (because I think that it is a slightly less dirty way of doing the
> > > same thing, as it wouldn't change the rownames permanently):
> > >
> > > \documentclass{article}
> > >
> > > \begin{document}
> > >
> > > <<results='asis'>>=
> > > tab <- matrix(rnorm(4), nrow=2)
> > > rownames(tab) <- c("a", "[b]c")
> > > colnames(tab) <- c("p", "q")
> > >
> > > library(xtable)
> > > print(xtable(tab),
> > >   sanitize.rownames.function=function(x) { gsub("^\\[", "\n\\[", x) }
> > > )
> > > @
> > > \end{document}
> > >
> > > So, my questions are:
> > >
> > > 1. Is there a more elegant way (or a more automatic way) of solving this
> > > issue?
> > > 2. If my workaround is reasonable, how should I fix my
> > > sanitize.rownames.function?
> > >
> > > Thanks a lot in advance.
> > >
> > > Best regards,
> > > Gopal

messages.subject: Managing a large document with LaTeX and knitr includeonly functions
messages.subject_clean: Managing a large document with LaTeX and knitr includeonly functions
messages.body_plain:
I am preparing a large multi-part document. In my main document (b.Rnw) I have (as Yihui suggested):

<<includeonly, echo = FALSE>>=
includeonly = function(file) {
includes = c('baFile', 'bbFile')
if (file %in% includes) paste0(file, '.Rnw')
}
@
<<ba, child = includeonly('baFile')>>=
@
<<bb, child = includeonly('bbFile')>>=
@

In order to use LaTeX's \includeonly function, I need to write
\includeonly(baFile.tex, bbFile.tex)

and then
\include{bbFile}

to produce only one part, but with cross-references intact.

So I need the includeonly function to also specify that the name of each output .tex file is of the form (e.g.) bbFile.tex.

Can this be done?

Thanks,
Michael
